LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 3.3.2 NON- FICTION: PERSONAL JOURNAL

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 3.3.2 Non- Fiction: Personal Journal
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 3.3.2 Non- Fiction: Personal Journal, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to keep journals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 3.3.2 Non- Fiction: Personal Journal together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: This is nurtured as the learner adapts new ideas that inspire creativity as they make an entry

of a personal journal from personal experiences.

Values:
Peace: This is enhanced as the learner displays tolerance with peers when working jointly to search for information on

stylistic devices used in personal journals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-awareness: This is promoted as the learner interacts with personal journals from various sources and keeps their

own.
